The One Big Beautiful Bill’s Medicaid and SNAP “protections” are bureaucratic theater. The bill’s work requirements (80 hours/month for Medicaid expansion adults) and eligibility redeterminations every six months create a maze of red tape that’ll kick millions off rolls—not just fraudsters. CBO projects 11 million losing coverage, with states like Arizona facing 21% Medicaid funding cuts.

Centralized SSN tracking and death-file checks? Classic D.C. overreach. Real reform would audit pharma overcharges and hospital price-gouging, not punish struggling families.

This bill doesn’t fix waste—it weaponizes complexity against the vulnerable while letting corporate middlemen keep fleecing the system.

Congress is selling “accountability” while quietly gutting coverage—see the receipts: https://t.co/4LNfUKzqzv

The FY26 NDAA's focus on military family support is a step forward, but real accountability means tracking every dollar. While the bill boosts pay and healthcare, Congress must ensure funds aren’t lost in bureaucratic bloat. For example, H.R. 4016’s $5M blast overpressure analysis (Sec. 3bb8ca8c) is critical, but DOD’s track record on timely implementation remains questionable.

Housing upgrades? Necessary. Childcare expansions? Vital. Yet without strict audits, these “investments” risk becoming line items in a ledger of waste.

Prioritize outcomes, not just allocations. Troops deserve efficiency, not empty promises.
